texts.preamble: Lokesh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 23 January, 2025 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.5829/2023 Kabc0B0141272023 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru.
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 09.07.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 09.07.2023 at about 01.30 p.m., petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 53-EL-7689 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding on Bangalore-Kolar NH-75 service Road, Tavarekere village, near Lotasas School, at that time the driver of JCB bearing Reg. No. KA-53-MJ-4084 drove in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner. Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 33 years, the petitioner was working as a Farmer and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared before this court and filed their respective written statements. The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending JCB. Lokesh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 23 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164406816/ 2 Further, this respondent no.1 not admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident. Further this respondent no.1 submits that, the petitioner was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident. The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and submitted that, the petitioner was driving the two-wheeler in a rash and negligent manner and came in a wrong direction and dashed the vehicle belonging to the 2nd respondent and hence the petitioner is responsible for causing the alleged accident. It is further submitted that, the petitioner was not having a valid driving license to drive the two-wheeler and he was not wearing helmet at the time of driving and came in wrong direction and dashed the vehicle of the respondent No.2 which was parked. Further, both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.16 and also examined Dr. Nagaraj B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.17 and 18 and closed their side. On the other hand, respondent No.1 examined its Legal Executive as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW.2.
texts.arguments: 15. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.79,701/- towards medical expenses. Lokesh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 23 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164406816/ 5 Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was a farmer and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document before this court. So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench. The accident is of the year is 2023. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-p.m. as per above decision. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
